**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.bom_multi_level`

**One row is** One child-to-parent line of a deep bill of materials: this material is consumed by this higher-level component, at this level of the tree. Collapsed to effective product-to-material arcs before the engine sees it. NOT deduplicated (D5).

**Resolution** — how a value is decided when more than one source could supply one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default mode | `asserted` |
| Assertable by | `csv_upload` |
| Estimable from | **never** — this value may not be estimated |
| Hybrid (centre / spread) | **none** — the engine has no variability field for this quantity |
| On conflict | `assertion_wins` |

estimable_from is EMPTY and that is a positive statement, not an omission. This is an engineering or commercial fact that someone knows exactly — it is written on a drawing, in a contract, or on a machine's nameplate. Fitting a distribution to it would produce a number with error bars around something that has no error, and the error bars would be believed. A future estimator reading this contract must refuse this field. Same rule as bom_single_level.consumption_rate, and more important here: multi-level rates multiply down the tree, so an estimate at level 3 propagates into every product above it.
